Dear Secretary Reese:

Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc. (“EGTS”) hereby submits, pursuant to Section

Energy Regulatory Commission (“Commission” or “FERC”), this Abbreviated Application
(“Application”) requesting the authority of a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity
for EGTS to construct, operate and maintain certain facilities located in Beaver, Clinton,
Lawrence, Potter, and Tioga Counties, Pennsylvania that comprise Project Stratum
(“Project”).

Information Submitted

This Application consists of the following volumes:

       Volume I:       Public
       Volume II:      Public
       Volume III:     CUI//PRIV Information – Do Not Release
       Volume IV:      CUI//CEII Information – Do Not Release

as privileged and confidential, and that it not be released to the public. This volume is labeled
“CUI//PRIV– Do Not Release” and contains information that is customarily treated as
privileged and confidential.

as Critical Energy Infrastructure Information (CEII), and that it is not released to the public.
This volume is labeled “CUI//CEII – Do Not Release” and contains information that is
customarily treated as CEII.

                                     Project Stratum


         Pursuant to Section 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act 1 (“NGA”), as amended, and the

regulations under Part 157 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission 2

(“Commission” or “FERC”), Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc. (“EGTS”),

hereby submits this Abbreviated Application for a Certificate of Public Convenience and

Necessity (“Application”) authorizing EGTS to construct, operate and maintain certain

facilities located in Beaver, Clinton, Lawrence, Potter, and Tioga Counties,

Pennsylvania. Specifically, EGTS proposes to construct and operate (i) 16 miles of 24-

inch pipeline, (ii) a new metering and regulation (M&R) facility, and (iii) improvements to

an existing compressor station. The proposed facilities comprise Project Stratum (the

“Project”) and will enable EGTS to provide 250,000 dekatherms per day (Dth/d) of

incremental firm natural gas transportation service.

         The Project’s capacity is fully subscribed by one long-term customer, Seneca

Resources Company, LLC (the “Project Customer”), commencing in November 2028.

The Project also provides numerous benefits to EGTS’ existing customers, and satisfies

the Commission’s guidelines set forth in the Statement of Policy Regarding Certification



1 15 U.S.C. § 717 (f).

2 18 C.F.R. Part 157 (2026).




                                        Page 1 of 12
 of New Interstate Natural Gas Pipeline Facilities. 3 Specifically, the Project will: (i)

provide increased natural gas firm transportation service; (ii) result in no financial

subsidy by existing customers; and (iii) have minimal adverse impacts on existing

customers, existing pipelines, or landowners and communities. As demonstrated herein,

the Project benefits outweigh the minimal residual impacts attributable to the Project,

and the Project is required by the present and future public convenience and necessity.

EGTS respectfully requests that the Commission issue a final order authorizing the

Project by November 6, 2027, in order to meet the Project Customer’s requested in-

service date of November 2028.

                          III.   DESCRIPTION OF PROPOSAL

          The Project will enable EGTS to provide transportation and delivery outlets for an

additional 250,000 Dth/d of natural gas production from Tioga County, Pennsylvania for

delivery to Lawrence and Clinton Counties, Pennsylvania. The Project utilizes targeted,

innovative enhancements of existing natural gas infrastructure to provide incremental

firm transportation service, in a market region that is experiencing increased natural gas

production activity and limited outlets for the produced gas. Through this enhancement,

the Project will expand access to attractively priced, natural gas pricing hubs for the

Project Customer.


A. Open Season

          From September 30 through October 10, 2025, EGTS conducted a binding open

season, seeking customer interest to enter into a binding firm transportation agreement

for the Project capacity. EGTS and the Project Customer had previously negotiated a

mutually acceptable Precedent Agreement for all available Project capacity, subject to

the results of the Open Season. The Project Customer was deemed as the winning

bidder through the Open Season process.



                                         Page 3 of 12
 B. Facilities and Operation

        EGTS proposes to construct and operate the facilities listed below. See Exhibit F

and Exhibit F-I for Project facility locations and for more detailed facility descriptions.

Pipeline Facilities

    •   TL-669 Natural Gas Transmission Line: install approximately 1.8 miles of 24-inch

        diameter pipeline parallel to the existing EGTS LN-25 and LN-35 pipelines in

        Beaver County, Pennsylvania

   •    TL-668 Natural Gas Transmission Line: install approximately 13.8 miles of 24-

        inch diameter pipeline via lift and lay installation (i.e., removal and replacement of

        existing pipe) in Clinton and Potter Counties, Pennsylvania

Existing Aboveground Facilities

   •    Sabinsville Station Improvements: complete improvements at the existing

        Sabinsville Station, including modifications to station piping, pressure control

        systems, miscellaneous pipeline components and valves, and supporting

        infrastructure in Tioga County, Pennsylvania

   •    Leidy Station Tie-In: install a new tie-in facility that will connect the proposed TL-

        668 pipeline to the existing TL-454 and LN-50 pipelines and include

        launcher/receivers and associated appurtenances in Clinton County,

        Pennsylvania

   •    Greenlick Station Tie-in: install new zone measurement equipment, a mainline

        valve assembly, and tie-ins to existing Greenlick Station piping in Potter County,

        Pennsylvania

    •   Koppel Junction Improvements: install a new launcher/receiver unit, mainline

        valve assembly, and a tie-in from the proposed TL-669 pipeline to the existing

        LN-25, LN-35, and TL-400 pipelines in Beaver County, Pennsylvania



                                         Page 4 of 12
 New Aboveground Facilities

    •   New Terrain M&R Facility and Pipeline Tap: install a new M&R facility and

        interconnect to existing LN-25 and LN-35 pipelines in Lawrence County,

        Pennsylvania

    •   Pine Mountain Gate Facility: install a new gate facility to include a new tie-in from

        the proposed TL-668 pipeline to the existing LN-50 pipeline, a launcher/receiver

        unit, and mainline valve assembly in Potter County, Pennsylvania

    •   Eaglerock Gate Facility: install a new gate facility to include a new tie-in from the

        proposed TL-669 pipeline to the existing LN-25 and LN-35 pipelines, and a

        launcher/receiver unit in Beaver County, Pennsylvania

C. Cost

        As detailed in Exhibit K, the estimated total Project cost is $163 million. The

Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (“AFUDC”) included in Exhibit K has

been calculated in compliance with Commission Policy. 4 EGTS affirms that it began to

incur capital expenditures for the Project in November 2025, and that activities

necessary to prepare the Project for its intended use were in progress at that time.

D. Market

        As detailed in Exhibit I, EGTS executed a binding Precedent Agreement with its

long-term Project Customer representing a full commitment for the 250,000 Dth/d of firm

transportation capacity created by the Project. The Project Customer will enter into a

service agreement to receive firm transportation service, commencing by November 1,

2028. Service will be provided under the terms and conditions of EGTS’ existing Rate

Schedule FT.

E. Initial Rate


4 Southern Natural Gas Co., 130 FERC ¶ 61,193 (2010).




                                            Page 5 of 12
          As shown in Exhibit P, EGTS has designed an initial incremental firm

transportation base reservation rate to recover costs of the Project facilities. The

proposed incremental base reservation rate reflects the estimated cost of the Project

facilities recovered over the incremental billing determinants. As shown in Exhibit P, the

incrementally-calculated firm transportation base reservation rate is higher than EGTS’

firm transportation system reservation rate proposed in Docket No. RP26-939, and the

incrementally-calculated usage rate for the Project capacity is less than EGTS’ firm

transportation usage rate. 5 Therefore, using the higher incremental base reservation

rate for services created by the Project will prevent existing customers from subsidizing

the incremental transportation service. Thus, EGTS’ proposed Project rates are

consistent with Commission Policy. 6

         EGTS has agreed to a fixed negotiated firm transportation base reservation rate

for the sole customer. 7 In addition to the negotiated base reservation rate, EGTS will

charge the base usage rate and all other applicable rates, charges and surcharges then

applicable to service under EGTS’ Rate Schedule FT, such as Transportation Cost Rate

Adjustment (TCRA) and Electric Power Cost Adjustment (EPCA) charges and system-

wide fuel retention. EGTS acknowledges that it must file for separate Commission

authorization of the negotiated rates, prior to commencing service. 8

                        IV.   PUBLIC CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY

          The Project is required by the present and future public convenience and

necessity. The benefits of the Project outweigh any adverse impacts on customers,

captive customers of other pipelines, or affected landowners and communities,

consistent with the Commission’s Policy Statement. By applying the Policy Statement

framework, the Commission seeks to foster competitive markets, to protect captive

customers, and to provide “incentives for the optimal level of construction and efficient

customer choice.” 9 The Project meets each of the Commission’s objectives.

A. The Threshold Requirement – No Financial Subsidies

          Under the Policy Statement, the threshold requirement is that a project must be

financially viable without any subsidies from existing customers. 10 EGTS has met this

requirement. As discussed in Section III.E. above, the incrementally-calculated base

reservation rate applicable to the Project is higher than EGTS’ existing firm

transportation system reservation rate, while the incrementally-calculated usage rate is

less than EGTS’ existing firm transportation system usage rate. Because the Project will

be charged the higher incremental reservation rate, EGTS’ existing customers will not

subsidize the Project.

B. No Adverse Effects on Potentially Affected Interests

          In deciding whether this proposal is required by the public convenience and

necessity, the Commission will consider any adverse effects on the economic interests

of existing EGTS customers, of competing pipelines and their captive customers, and of

landowners and surrounding communities. This proposal will have no adverse effect on

existing EGTS customers or on any competing pipeline and its captive customers.



9 Policy Statement at p. 61,743.

10 Id. at p. 61,746.




                                         Page 7 of 12
 EGTS has designed the Project to eliminate or minimize the already-limited adverse

impacts of Project construction and operation on the environment, affected landowners,

and communities. Any residual impact on these interests is outweighed by the public

benefits associated with this Project.

       1. No Adverse Effects on EGTS Customers

       The Project will not adversely affect existing EGTS customers; existing

customers will not experience a cost increase or degradation in service. To the extent

that the Project facilities deliver incremental natural gas supply into an otherwise fully-

subscribed portion of its system, the Project offers potential benefits to its customers.

       2. No Adverse Effects on Captive Customers of Other Pipelines

       The Project will not affect the captive customers of other existing pipelines in this

region because the proposed facilities are designed to create incremental capacity on a

portion of the EGTS system. This new capacity will provide an additional outlet for

production in the area. Rather than supplant existing service to customers that currently

utilize transportation service from other pipeline systems, the Project will increase

natural gas supply available into both EGTS and neighboring systems.

       3. Minimizing Adverse Effects on Affected Landowners and Communities

       The Project has been designed to minimize impact to landowners, communities

and the environment. All facility installations will be on land that EGTS will own, lease or

hold a property interest in to support the natural gas facilities. The majority of the

pipeline installations will parallel existing EGTS pipelines LN-50, and LN-25/LN-35, and

EGTS currently holds substantially all the required rights of way. A list of landowners

whose property may be affected by construction is included in Exhibit F-I (Volume III).

EGTS will provide landowner notification in accordance with 18 C.F.R. § 157.6(d). If any

affected landowners have concerns related to the Project, EGTS will work cooperatively

with them to address their concerns.

                                         Page 8 of 12
 C. The Benefits of the Project Outweigh the Adverse Impacts

       EGTS has entered into a binding Precedent Agreement with a long-term, non-

affiliated Project Customer for the entire Project capacity, for 15 years. The firm

transportation service provided by the Project will serve unmet demand for natural gas-

fueled electric generation, and is expected to enhance the reliability of the electric grid

and help mitigate costs for consumers. The Project will serve demand for incremental

home heating, commercial, and industrial uses in Pennsylvania, Ohio, West Virginia and

markets in the Midwest, Northeast and Mid-Atlantic. Moreover, the Project will have

limited – if any – adverse impact on existing customers, other pipelines and their captive

customers, and affected landowners and communities. The Project meets the

Commission’s requirements in the Certificate Policy Statement and is required by the

present and future public convenience and necessity. As such, the benefits of the

Project clearly outweigh any potential residual adverse effects.

                              VI.     ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT

        As shown in Exhibit F-I (Volume II), construction and operation of the Project

facilities are not expected to have a significant adverse impact on the quality of human

health or the environment. The facilities have been designed to minimize or mitigate any

environmental or other adverse impacts. As such, an environmental impact statement is

not necessary for this Project to satisfy the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969. 11



                                         VII.    NOTICE

        A form of notice suitable for publication in the Federal Register is attached.



            VIII.    REQUESTED AUTHORIZATION AND CONCLUSION

        EGTS respectfully requests that the Commission accept this Abbreviated

Application for filing; publish notice of this Application in the Federal Register; and issue

an Order by November 6, 2027, authorizing EGTS to undertake the Project as proposed.

        EGTS requests that the Commission process this Application in accordance with

the shortened procedures set forth in Rules 801 and 802 of the Commission’s Rules of

Practice and Procedure and omit the intermediate decision procedures. If the

         Take notice that on November 6, 2026, Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage,
Inc. (EGTS), 10700 Energy Way, Glen Allen, VA 23060, filed an application under
section 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act (NGA), and Part 157 of the Commission’s regulations
requesting authorization for Project Stratum (Project). EGTS proposes installing
approximately 1.8 miles of 24-inch diameter pipeline (TL-669) parallel to the existing
EGTS LN-25/LN-35 pipelines in Beaver County, PA; installing approximately 13.8 miles
of 24-inch diameter pipeline (TL-668) via lift and lay installation in Clinton and Potter
Counties, PA; constructing a new greenfield Metering and Regulation (M&R) facility
(New Terrain) in Lawrence County, PA; and improving existing EGTS infrastructure at its
Sabinsville Station in Tioga County, PA. The Project’s proposed facilities will create an
incremental 250,000 dekatherms per day (Dth/d) from receipt points at Tioga County, PA
for deliveries to Lawrence and Clinton Counties, PA.

       PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

        There are three ways to become involved in the Commission’s review of this
project: you can file a protest to the project, you can file a motion to intervene in the
proceeding, and you can file comments on the project. There is no fee or cost for filing
protests, motions to intervene, or comments. The deadline for filing protests, motions to
intervene, and comments is 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on December __, 2026. How to file
protests, motions to intervene, and comments is explained below.

        The Commission’s Office of Public Participation (OPP) supports meaningful
public engagement and participation in Commission proceedings. OPP can help
members of the public, including landowners, environmental justice communities, Tribal
members and others, access publicly available information and navigate Commission
processes. For public inquiries and assistance with making filings such as interventions,
comments, or requests for rehearing, the public is encouraged to contact OPP at
(202) 502-6595 or OPP@ferc.gov.

       Comments

        Any person wishing to comment on the project may do so. Comments may
include statements of support or objections, to the project as a whole or specific aspects
of the project. The more specific your comments, the more useful they will be.

       Protests

        Pursuant to sections 157.10(a)(4) 2 and 385.211 3 of the Commission’s regulations
under the NGA, any person 4 may file a protest to the application. Protests must comply
with the requirements specified in section 385.2001 5 of the Commission’s regulations. A
protest may also serve as a motion to intervene so long as the protestor states it also

                                                MARKET DATA
                                                     1
         In its Certificate Policy Statement , the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission

found that Precedent Agreements are “significant evidence of demand” to support the

approval of natural gas infrastructure projects. Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc.

(EGTS) provides below a summary of the relevant terms of the Precedent Agreement with

its Project Customer.

         Market Support

         The long-term Project Customer has executed a binding Precedent Agreement

representing a 100% market commitment for the 250,000 dekatherms per day (Dth/d) of firm

transportation capacity that is created by the Project.

         The primary receipt points for the Project Customer originate from existing receipt

point locations on the EGTS system in Tioga County, Pennsylvania, with deliveries directed

to an existing interconnection between EGTS and Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line

Corporation in Clinton County, Pennsylvania, and a new interconnection between the

Pipeline and Tennessee Gas Pipeline in Lawrence County, Pennsylvania. The Project

provides firm reliable transportation of natural gas from production receipts in the Tioga

County area to attractive and liquid natural gas pricing hubs in Pennsylvania and Ohio.

Natural gas is sourced from these pricing hubs for power generation, home heating, and

industrial uses in Pennsylvania, Ohio and West Virginia. The Project capacity will provide

greater reliability for the Project Customer to flow production gas from its location in Tioga

County to liquid supply points on the EGTS pipeline system.

       Seneca Resources is the Anchor Shipper on the Project and has significant

production in the Northeast/Tioga region estimated at 1.1 Bcf/d (January 2026). Seneca

Resources currently maintains approximately 1 Bcf/d of firm transportation capacity through

several interconnections with major interstate pipeline systems, enabling reliable access to

several market destinations. As production from its Pennsylvania assets continues to grow,

Seneca Resources has identified the need for additional takeaway capacity and anticipates

contracting for additional firm transportation capacity totaling an estimated 1.5 million Dth/d

of firm transportation by 2030. The incremental capacity being developed in Project Stratum

will aid Seneca Resources' long-term growth strategy, providing the pipeline infrastructure

needed to support its expanding production and providing access to premium downstream

markets.

       Project Stratum will help position Seneca Resources to meet these future

transportation requirements by expanding access to growing demand centers across

Pennsylvania, the Mid-Atlantic region, and the Gulf Coast.

       By providing additional firm transportation opportunities, Project Stratum enhances

Seneca Resources’ long-term marketing portfolio, supports the development of its Tioga-

area inventory, improves access to premium-priced markets, and reduces risk of interruption

to gas flow from production areas.

       In summary, the project will provide a reliable, price-competitive natural gas outlet for

the benefit of the Project Customer, while providing downstream access to natural gas for

eventual end-use for power generation, home heating, and commercial/industrial uses.

terminating the above-captioned proceeding, this Protective Agreement shall remain in
effect until the earlier of: (i) termination by mutual agreement of the Parties; (ii) an order of
the Commission terminating this Protective Agreement; or (iii) the date that an order
terminating the above-captioned proceeding becomes no longer subject to judicial review.

2.      This Protective Agreement applies to the following two categories of materials: (A)
materials that EGTS may designate as protected that EGTS customarily treats as sensitive
or proprietary, that are not available to the public, and that, if disclosed freely, would subject
EGTS, its customers or parties with which EGTS has a contractual relationship to a risk of
competitive disadvantage or other business injury; and (B) materials that contain critical
energy infrastructure information, as defined in 18 CFR§ 388.113(c)(1) ("Critical Energy
Infrastructure Information" or “CEII”).




                                           Page 1 of 9
                                                          Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc.
                                                                                   Project Stratum
                                                                         Docket No. CP27-___-000

3.     Definitions -- For purposes of this Protective Agreement:

        (a) The term "Protected Materials" means (1) materials submitted to the Commission
on November 6, 2026 in the above-captioned proceeding for which EGTS requested
privileged treatment pursuant to the Commission’s regulations and any subsequent
submissions by EGTS to the Commission in the above-captioned proceeding for which
EGTS request privileged treatment pursuant to the Commission’s regulations, provided
however, that material specified in 18 C.F.R. §388.112(b)(2)(vi) must be sought pursuant to
a Freedom of Information Act or Critical Energy Infrastructure Information request; (2) any
information contained in or obtained from such designated materials; (3) any other materials
which are made subject to this Protective Agreement by the Commission, by any court or
other body having appropriate authority, or by mutual written agreement of the Parties; (4)
Notes of Protected Materials (as defined below); and (5) copies of Protected Materials.
When producing Protected Materials, EGTS shall physically mark them on each page as
"CUI/PRIV" or with a designation of similar import to indicate that they are Protected
Materials. If the Protected Materials contain Critical Energy Infrastructure Information, then
when producing such information, EGTS shall additionally mark on each page containing
such information the words "CUI/CEII -- Do Not Release."

         (b) The term "Notes of Protected Materials" means memoranda, handwritten notes,
or any other form of information (including electronic form) that copy or disclose materials
described in Paragraph 3(a)(1). Notes of Protected Materials are subject to the same
restrictions as other Protected Materials, except as specifically provided in this Protective
Agreement.

        (c) Protected Materials shall not include: (1) any information or document that has
been filed with and accepted into the public files of the Commission, or contained in the
public files of any other federal or state agency, or any federal or state court, unless the
information or document has been determined to be protected by such agency or court, or
(2) information that is public knowledge, or which becomes public knowledge, other than
through disclosure in violation of this Protective Agreement or another Protective Agreement
to which EGTS is a party. Protected Materials do include any information or document
contained in the files of the Commission that has been designated as Critical Energy
Infrastructure Information.

        (d) The terms “Non-Disclosure Certificate Concerning Protected Material” and “Non-
Disclosure Certificate Concerning Protected Material Including Protected Material Marked as
Not Available to Competitive Duty Personnel” shall mean the certificates annexed hereto
that, once signed by each Reviewing Representative of Participant, will allow for access to
Protected Materials and shall certify the Reviewing Representative’s understanding that
such access to Protected Materials is provided pursuant to the terms and restrictions of this
Protective Agreement, and that such Reviewing Representative has read and understands
the Protective Agreement and agrees to be bound by it.

      (e) The term "Reviewing Representative" shall mean a person who has signed a
Non-Disclosure Certificate and who is:

       (1) an attorney who is representing Participant in the above-captioned proceeding;

       (2) attorneys, paralegals and other employees associated for purposes of the above-
           captioned proceeding with an attorney described in Subparagraph (1);


                                          Page 2 of 9
                                                           Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc.
                                                                                    Project Stratum
                                                                          Docket No. CP27-___-000


       (3) an expert or an employee of an expert retained by Participant or attorney for
           Participant for the purpose of advising, preparing for or testifying in the above-
           captioned proceeding;

       (4) employees of Participant with primary responsibility to represent Participant’s
           interest in the above-captioned proceeding; or

       (5) a person designated as a Reviewing Representative by order of the Commission.

4.      Protected Materials shall be made available under the terms of this Protective
Agreement only to Participant and only through Participant’s Reviewing Representatives as
provided in Paragraphs 7-9 below. Participant shall provide EGTS with a written request for
the specific Protected Materials it wishes to obtain subject to this Protective Agreement,
including the FERC Accession number and applicable date. Such request shall not be
deemed to create a continuing obligation on the part of EGTS to provide additional
Protected Materials.

5.     Protected Materials shall remain available to Participant (or, pursuant to Paragraph
20 below, shall remain available for Participant’s review) until the date that an order
terminating the above-captioned proceeding becomes no longer subject to judicial review. If
requested to do so by EGTS in writing after that date, Participant shall, within fifteen days of
such request, return the Protected Materials to EGTS, or shall destroy the materials, except
that copies of filings, official transcripts and exhibits in the above-captioned proceeding that
contain Protected Materials, and Notes of Protected Material may be retained, if they are
maintained in accordance with Paragraph 6, below. Within such time period Participant, if
requested to do so, shall also submit to EGTS an affidavit stating that, to the best of its
knowledge, all Protected Materials and all Notes of Protected Materials have been returned
or have been destroyed or will be maintained in accordance with Paragraph 6. To the extent
Protected Materials are not returned or destroyed, they shall remain subject to the
Protective Agreement and may not be used in any other proceeding or forum other than in
the above-captioned proceeding.

6.      All Protected Materials shall be maintained by the Participant in a secure place.
Protected Materials shall be treated as confidential by the Participant and by the Reviewing
Representative in accordance with the Non-Disclosure Certificate(s) executed pursuant to
Paragraph 9. Participant shall exercise at least the same degree of care with respect to the
Protected Materials as Participant uses in handling its own confidential information. Access
to Protected Materials shall be limited to those Reviewing Representatives specifically
authorized pursuant to Paragraphs 8-9. Participant shall be responsible and liable for any
breach of this Protective Agreement by it or any of the Reviewing Representatives whether
the Protected Materials are provided directly or indirectly by EGTS or Participant.

7.      Reviewing Representatives may make copies of Protected Materials, so long as
Reviewing Representative maintains adequate records of all copies made and distributed,
but such copies become Protected Materials. Reviewing Representatives may make notes
of Protected Materials, which shall be treated as Notes of Protected Materials.

8.     (a) Protected Materials shall not be used except as necessary in the above-
captioned proceeding.



                                          Page 3 of 9
                                                           Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc.
                                                                                    Project Stratum
                                                                          Docket No. CP27-___-000

        (b) Under no circumstances can a Reviewing Representative use information
contained in any Protected Materials obtained under the Protective Agreement to give
Participant, Participant’s affiliates, any competitor of EGTS, or any other entity a commercial
advantage.

        (c) Subject to Paragraphs 20 and 21 regarding access to Protected Materials that are
marked as “Not Available to Competitive Duty Personnel,” in the event that Participant
wishes to designate as a Reviewing Representative a person not described in Paragraph
3(e) above, Participant shall provide EGTS with the name, affiliation and a description of the
job duties and responsibilities related to the above-captioned proceeding for each individual
requesting to become a Reviewing Representative. If EGTS consents, that person shall be a
Reviewing Representative pursuant to Paragraph 3(e) above with respect to those
materials. If no agreement is reached, Participant may submit the disputed designation to
the Commission for resolution.

9.      A Reviewing Representative shall not be permitted to inspect, participate in
discussions regarding, or otherwise be permitted access to Protected Materials pursuant to
this Protective Agreement unless that Reviewing Representative has first executed a Non-
Disclosure Certificate and provided a copy to counsel for EGTS.

10.     Subject to Paragraph 17, the Commission shall resolve any disputes arising under
this Protective Agreement. If Participant contests EGTS’s designation of materials as
protected, it shall notify EGTS by specifying in writing the materials the designation of which
is contested. Prior to presenting any dispute under this Protective Agreement to the
Commission, the parties to the dispute shall use their best efforts to resolve it. The
procedures described in this Paragraph shall not apply to Protected Materials designated by
EGTS as Critical Energy Infrastructure Information. Materials so designated shall remain
protected and subject to the provisions of this Protective Agreement unless Participant
requests and obtains a determination from the Commission's Critical Energy Infrastructure
Information Coordinator that such materials need not remain protected.

11.     All documents or copies thereof reflecting Protected Materials, including any
documents that contain or refer to Protected Materials, in the event they are filed with the
Commission, shall be filed either (i) by hand in sealed envelopes or other appropriate
containers endorsed to the effect that they contain Protected Materials; or (ii) electronically
on the Commission’s website in accordance with the procedures for electronic filing of
privileged material or CEII. Such documents shall be marked "CUI/PRIV" and shall be filed
under seal and served in accordance with the Commission’s regulations. Such documents
containing Critical Energy Infrastructure Information shall be additionally marked "CUI/CEII -
- Do Not Release." For anything filed by hand or electronically, redacted versions or, where
an entire document is protected, a letter indicating such, will also be filed with the
Commission and served in accordance with the Commission’s regulations. Participant and
its counsel shall take all reasonable precautions necessary to assure that Protected
Materials are not distributed to unauthorized persons.

12.     Except in cases where release is ordered sooner by the Commission, and subject to
the conditions on release of Protected Materials that are marked as “Not Available to
Competitive Duty Personnel” set forth in Paragraph 20, Protected Materials that have been
requested pursuant to this Protective Agreement will be made available within fifteen days of
receipt of the request satisfying 18 C.F.R. § 388.112(b)(2)(iii); provided, however, that if
EGTS files an objection to such request with the Commission, EGTS is under no obligation


                                          Page 4 of 9
                                                            Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc.
                                                                                     Project Stratum
                                                                           Docket No. CP27-___-000

to disclose the requested Protected Materials until ordered by the Commission or a
decisional authority.

13.     Nothing in this Protective Agreement shall be construed as precluding EGTS or
Participant from objecting to the use of Protected Materials on any legal grounds.

14.    Nothing in this Protective Agreement shall preclude Participant from requesting the
Commission to find that this Protective Agreement should not apply to all or any materials
previously designated as Protected Materials pursuant to this Protective Agreement. The
Commission may alter or amend this Protective Agreement as circumstances warrant at any
time during the course of the above-captioned proceeding. The Parties may amend this
Protective Agreement at any time by written mutual agreement without seeking Commission
approval, unless such amendment is otherwise specifically prohibited by law.

15.   Both EGTS and Participant have the right to seek changes in this Protective
Agreement from the Commission.

16.      If the Commission finds at any time in the course of the above-captioned proceeding
that all or part of the Protected Materials need not be protected, those materials shall
nevertheless be subject to the protection afforded by this Protective Agreement until the
date that the Commission orders the materials be produced. EGTS reserves its rights to
seek additional administrative or judicial remedies after the Commission’s decision
respecting Protected Materials or Reviewing Representatives, or the Commission's denial of
any request for rehearing thereof. The provisions of 18 CFR §§ 388.112 and 388.113 shall
apply to any requests under the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552) for Protected
Materials in the files of the Commission.

17.    Nothing in this Protective Agreement shall be deemed to preclude Participant or
EGTS from independently seeking through discovery in any other administrative or judicial
proceeding information or materials produced in the above-captioned proceeding under this
Protective Agreement.

18.    Neither EGTS nor Participant waive the right to pursue any other legal or equitable
remedies that may be available in the event of actual or anticipated disclosure of Protected
Materials.

19.     The contents of Protected Materials or any other form of information that copies or
discloses Protected Materials shall not be disclosed to anyone other than in accordance with
this Protective Agreement and shall be used only in connection with the above-captioned
proceeding.

20.     EGTS shall physically mark with the words “Not Available to Competitive Duty
Personnel,” any Protected Materials that EGTS believes in good faith would, if freely
disclosed, subject EGTS, or a third party, to risk of competitive disadvantage or other
concrete business injury if provided to all Reviewing Representatives. Such information may
include, but is not limited to (a) non-public business development, acquisition, or marketing
data, plans or activities; (b) non-public business or financial data, plans or activities; (c) any
non-public contractual terms; (d) negotiations of services, prices and rates; or (e) proprietary
information relating to process technology, engineering, design, or equipment related to the
above-captioned proceeding prepared by EGTS or any of their third party contractors, the
public disclosure of which EGTS in good faith believes would competitively harm EGTS or a


                                           Page 5 of 9
                                                         Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc.
                                                                                  Project Stratum
                                                                        Docket No. CP27-___-000

third party (hereafter “Market Sensitive Information”). Market Sensitive Information should
customarily be treated by the providing Participant as sensitive or proprietary and not be
available to the public. Any challenge to such a designation of Protected Materials may be
made as provided in this Protective Agreement. EGTS, in its discretion, may require that
Protected Materials designated “Not Available to Competitive Duty Personnel” be viewed on
site at the office of Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc. located at 10700 Energy
Way, Glen Allen, VA 23060.

21.     Solely with respect to Protected Materials that have been marked “Not Available to
Competitive Duty Personnel” and information derived therefrom, a Reviewing
Representative may not be any employee or agent of Participant whose duties include, on a
consistent and regular basis, (1) marketing, sale, or purchase of natural gas, natural gas
transportation or storage services; (2) management responsibility regarding, or the
supervision of any employee whose duties include marketing, sale, or purchase of natural
gas, natural gas transportation or storage services; (3) the provision of consulting services
regarding marketing, sale, or purchase of natural gas, natural gas transportation or storage
services; or (4) responsibility regarding other activities in which use of Market Sensitive
Information could be reasonably expected to cause competitive harm to EGTS or third party
(collectively, “Competitive Duties”). In the case of proprietary information as defined in
Paragraph 20(e) above, EGTS or any of its third party contractors may refuse to share such
proprietary information with any potential Reviewing Representative that they deem to be a
competitor. Under no circumstances shall a Reviewing Representative disclose any Market
Sensitive Information to any personnel unless such personnel follow the requirements
hereunder. In the event that (a) any person who has been a Reviewing Representative
subsequently is assigned to perform any Competitive Duties, or (b) previously available
Protected Materials are changed to “Not Available to Competitive Duty Personnel,” a
Reviewing Representative involved in Competitive Duties shall have no access to EGTS’
Protected Materials that are marked “Not Available to Competitive Duty Personnel” or
information derived therefrom. Such Reviewing Representative shall immediately dispose of
EGTS’ Protected Materials in his/her possession that are marked “Not Available to
Competitive Duty Personnel” and information derived therefrom and shall continue to
comply with the requirements of the Non-Disclosure Certificate Concerning Protected
Material, Including Protected Material Marked as Not Available to Competitive Duty
Personnel, and this Protective Agreement with respect to any Protected Materials to which
such person previously had access.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, with respect to Protected Materials that have been marked
“Not Available to Competitive Duty Personnel” and information derived therefrom, a
Reviewing Representative may not be an employee of a FERC-regulated natural gas
pipeline or storage facility in any region in which EGTS operates, or, if the Protected
Materials are third party proprietary information as defined in Section 20(e) above, an
employee of a competitor of such third party. Reviewing Representatives of such a pipeline,
or storage facility, with respect to Protected Materials that have been marked “Not Available
to Competitive Duty Personnel” shall be limited to outside counsel and/or consultants,
provided such individuals are not engaged in Competitive Duties as defined above on behalf
of such pipeline or storage facility.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, a person who otherwise would be disqualified as Competitive
Duty Personnel may serve as a Reviewing Representative upon agreement of EGTS or, in
the absence of such agreement, upon entry of an order of the Commission authorizing such
person to serve as a Reviewing Representative. Any request for an agreement or order

                                                              Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc.

under the preceding sentence shall be subject to the following conditions: (i) Participant
must certify in writing to EGTS that Participant’s ability to participate effectively in the above-
captioned proceeding would be prejudiced if it was unable to rely on the assistance of the
particular Reviewing Representative; (ii) Participant must identify by name and job title the
particular Reviewing Representative required and must describe the person’s duties and
responsibilities; (iii) the Participant claiming such prejudice must acknowledge in writing to
EGTS that access to the Protected Materials that are marked as Not Available to

adjudication of the above-captioned proceeding, absent prior written consent of EGTS or
authorization of the Commission with opportunity for EGTS to seek review of such decision
as provided in this Protective Agreement; (iv) Participant must acknowledge in writing that
any other use of Protected Materials which are Not Available to Competitive Duty Personnel
shall constitute a violation of this Protective Agreement; and (v) prior to having access to
any Protected Materials that are marked as Not Available to Competitive Duty Personnel,
the Competitive Duty Personnel who is authorized to act as a Reviewing Representative
must execute and deliver to EGTS a Non-Disclosure Certificate Concerning Protected
Material Including Protected Material Marked As Not Available to Competitive Duty
Personnel, acknowledging his or her familiarity with the contents of this Protective
Agreement and the particular restrictions set forth in this paragraph regarding such
Protected Materials. Materials marked as “Not Available to Competitive Duty Personnel”
and/or notes from a review of the Protected Materials marked as “Not Available to
Competitive Duty Personnel” shall be returned or destroyed at the conclusion of the above-
captioned proceeding as otherwise provided in this Protective Agreement.

22.      If EGTS believes that Protected Materials previously disclosed to Reviewing
Representative(s) contain Market Sensitive Information, public disclosure of which would
competitively harm EGTS, and should be treated as if such Protected Materials had been
labeled “Not Available to Competitive Duty Personnel,” EGTS shall notify Participant. In such

“Not Available to Competitive Duty Personnel,” it will be the responsibility of Participant to
ensure compliance with this Protective Agreement after the additional designation; EGTS
will not be responsible for redistributing or re-labeling the affected Protected Materials.

9.   Describe and provide location maps of all jurisdictional facilities, including all aboveground          Section 1.3, Appendix 1-A
     facilities associated with the project (such as: meter stations, pig launchers/receivers,
     valves), to be constructed, modified, abandoned, replaced, or removed, including related
     construction and operational support activities and areas such as maintenance bases,
     staging areas, communications towers, power lines, and new access roads (roads to be
     built or modified). As relevant, the report must describe the length and diameter of the
     pipeline, the types of aboveground facilities that would be installed, and associated land
     requirements. It must also identify other companies that must construct jurisdictional
     facilities related to the project, where the facilities would be located, and where they are in
     the Commission's approval process.
10. Identify and describe all non-jurisdictional facilities, including auxiliary facilities, that will be          Section 1.10
    built in association with the project, including facilities to be built by other companies.
    (i) Provide the following information:
     - (A) A brief description of each facility, including as appropriate: Ownership, land
           requirements, gas consumption, megawatt size, construction status, and an update of
           the latest status of federal, state, and local permits/approvals;
     - (B) The length and diameter of any interconnecting pipeline;
     - (C) Current 1:24,000/1:25,000 scale topographic maps showing the location of the
            facilities;
     - (D) Correspondence with the appropriate State Historic Preservation Officer (SHPO)
            or duly authorized Tribal Historic Preservation Officer (THPO) for tribal lands regarding
            whether properties eligible for listing on the National Register of Historic Places
            (NRHP) would be affected;
     - (E) Correspondence with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (and National Marine
            Fisheries Service, if appropriate) regarding potential impacts of the proposed facility
            on federally listed threatened and endangered species; and
     - (F) For facilities within a designated coastal zone management area, a consistency
            determination or evidence that the owner has requested a consistency determination
            from the state's coastal zone management program.
     (ii) Address each of the following factors and indicate which ones, if any, appear to indicate
     the need for the Commission to do an environmental review of project-related non-
     jurisdictional facilities.
     -      (A) Whether or not the regulated activity comprises “merely a link” in a corridor type
            project (e.g., a transportation or utility transmission project).
     -      (B) Whether there are aspects of the non-jurisdictional facility in the immediate vicinity
            of the regulated activity which uniquely determine the location and configuration of the
            regulated activity.
     -      (C) The extent to which the entire project will be within the Commission's jurisdiction.
     -      (D) The extent of cumulative federal control and responsibility.
 11. Provide the following maps and photos:
    - (i) Current, original United States Geological Survey (USGS) 7.5-minute series                             Appendix 1-A
         topographic maps or maps of equivalent detail, covering at least a 0.5-mile-wide
         corridor centered on the pipeline, with integer mileposts identified, showing the
         location of rights of way, new access roads, other linear construction areas,
         compressor stations, and pipe storage areas. Show nonlinear construction areas on
         maps at a scale of 1:3,600 or larger keyed graphically and by milepost to the right-of-
         way maps.
                                                                                                                 Appendix 1-B
    - (ii) Original aerial images or photographs or photo-based alignment sheets based on
         these sources, not more than 1 year old (unless older ones accurately depict current
         land use and development) and with a scale of 1:6,000 or larger, showing the
         proposed pipeline route and location of major aboveground facilities, covering at least
         a 0.5 mile-wide corridor, and including mileposts. Older images/photographs/
         alignment sheets should be modified to show any residences not depicted in the
         original. Alternative formats (e.g., blue-line prints of acceptable resolution) need prior
         approval by the environmental staff of the Office of Energy Projects.
    - (iii) In addition to the copy required under §157.6(a)(2) of this chapter, applicant should               Filed Separately
         send two additional copies of topographic maps and aerial images/photographs
         directly to the environmental staff of the Office of Energy Projects.
12. When new or additional compression is proposed, include large scale (1:3,600 or greater)                     Not Applicable
    plot plans of each compressor station. The plot plan should reference a readily identifiable
    point(s) on the USGS maps required in paragraph (c)(3) of this section. The maps and plot
    plans must identify the location of the nearest noise-sensitive areas (schools, hospitals, or
    residences) within 1 mile of the compressor station, existing and proposed compressor and
    auxiliary buildings, access roads, and the limits of areas that would be permanently
    disturbed.
13. (i) Identify facilities to be abandoned, and state how they would be abandoned, how the site                 Not Applicable
    would be restored, who would own the site or right of way after abandonment, and who
    would be responsible for any facilities abandoned in place.
     -     (ii) When the right of way or the easement would be abandoned, identify whether
           landowners were given the opportunity to request that the facilities on their property,
           including foundations and below ground components, be removed. Identify any
           landowners whose preferences the company does not intend to honor, and the
           reasons therefore.
14. Describe proposed construction and restoration methods to be used in areas of rugged                          Section 1.5
    topography, residential areas, active croplands, sites where the pipeline would be located
    parallel to and under roads, and sites where explosives are likely to be used.

15. Unless provided in response to Resource Report 5, describe estimated workforce                        Section 1.7, Resource Report
    requirements, including the number of pipeline construction spreads, average workforce                              5
    requirements for each construction spread and meter or compressor station, estimated
    duration of construction from initial clearing to final restoration, and number of personnel to
    be hired to operate the proposed project.
16. Describe reasonably foreseeable plans for future expansion of facilities, including additional                Section 1.11
    land requirements and the compatibility of those plans with the current proposal.
17. Describe all authorizations required to complete the proposed action and the status of                        Section 1.12
    applications for such authorizations. Identify environmental mitigation requirements
    specified in any permit or proposed in any permit application to the extent not specified
    elsewhere in this section.
18. Provide the names and mailing addresses of all affected landowners specified in §157.6(d)                    Appendix 1-G

 1.0        RESOURCE REPORT 1 – GENERAL PROJECT DESCRIPTION


 Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc. (EGTS) is seeking a Certificate of Public
 Convenience and Necessity (Certificate) from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC
 or Commission) under Section 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act (NGA), as amended, for the proposed
 Project Stratum (Project). As required by 18 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 380.12, EGTS
 is submitting this Environmental Report (ER) in support of its Application to the Commission for a
 Certificate to construct and operate the proposed Project facilities.

 1.1       PROPOSED FACILITIES

 EGTS proposes to construct and operate approximately 15.6 miles of new natural gas pipeline,
 two new gate facilities, one new metering and regulation (M&R) facility and pipeline tap, and
 improvements and modifications at three existing facilities in Beaver, Clinton, Lawrence, Potter,
 and Tioga Counties, Pennsylvania (PA) (see Figure 1.3-1). The Project is designed to provide
 250,000 dekatherms per day (Dth/d) of incremental, year-round firm natural gas transportation
 capacity to meet growing energy needs in PA and enhance the flexibility and reliability of the
 EGTS system. To provide the incremental capacity, EGTS will leverage existing infrastructure,
 including receipt point Metering and Regulation (M&R) facilities and compressor stations, in
 addition to installing new pipeline, completing upgrades at existing stations, and constructing new
 supporting facilities. The incremental capacity would support deliveries to Lawrence and Clinton
 Counties, PA.

 The Project will improve access to natural gas markets by supporting the efficient movement of
 natural gas from upstream production areas to downstream markets. The Project will enhance
 the reliability, resilience, and flexibility of the interstate pipeline network by strengthening market
 connectivity and supporting the reliable delivery of natural gas to utilities, power generators, and
 industrial customers.

 The proposed Project facilities include the following:

 Pipeline Facilities:
    • TL-669 Natural Gas Transmission Line: install approximately 1.8 miles of new 24-inch
        outside diameter steel natural gas pipeline originating from the existing Koppel Junction
        and extending northwest to the proposed Eaglerock Gate Facility in Beaver County, PA.
        The pipeline will be co-located with the existing EGTS LN-25 and LN-35 natural gas
        pipelines.
       •   TL-668 Natural Gas Transmission Line: install approximately 13.8 miles of new 24-inch
           outside diameter steel natural gas pipeline originating from a tie-in at the existing Leidy
           Station in Clinton County, PA to a tie-in at the proposed Pine Mountain Gate Facility in
           Potter County, PA. The pipeline will be co-located with several other EGTS pipelines and
           will replace the existing LN-280/LN-340 pipelines along the proposed TL-668 alignment.

 Existing Aboveground Facilities:
    • Sabinsville Station Improvements: complete various modifications and improvements at
        the existing Sabinsville Station to support the Project which may involve replacements,
        upgrades, or rearrangements of station piping, pressure control systems, miscellaneous
        pipeline components and valves, and supporting infrastructure. The proposed

1.2       PROJECT PURPOSE AND NEED

The Project is needed to provide additional firm natural gas transportation capacity to support
market demand and enhance the flexibility and reliability of the EGTS system. The Project will
create 250,000 Dth/d of incremental, year-round firm transportation capacity from existing receipt
points in Tioga County, PA for deliveries to Lawrence and Clinton Counties, PA.




                                                     -2-                                  Project Stratum
                                                                                          November 2026
 To support the incremental firm transportation capacity and deliveries, the Project will require
upgrades and improvements to existing EGTS infrastructure in addition to the installation of
pipeline looping and supporting facilities.

EGTS has executed a 15-year binding precedent agreement with its customer representing a full
market commitment for the entire volume of firm natural gas transportation capacity that will be
created by the Project. The Project customer will enter into a service agreement to receive firm
transportation service, commencing no earlier than November 1, 2028.

As demonstrated by macro-level projections from the U.S. Energy Information Administration
(EIA) Annual Energy Outlook 2026 (see Figure 1.2-1), domestic dry natural gas production is
projected to consistently expand across nearly all economic modeling scenarios, outstripping
standard baseline domestic consumption through the year 2050. In the Utica and Marcellus shale
plays spanning Ohio and PA, this surge in production creates a structural regional surplus that
requires modernized, expanded pipeline infrastructure to alleviate localized pipeline constraints
and prevent supply bottlenecks. Simultaneously, the EIA projections reflect a sustained, long-
term requirement for stable domestic consumption to support industrial manufacturing and grid
reliability across these key regional markets. To satisfy this macro-economic demand, the Project
has secured a binding precedent agreement for its capacity, establishing the direct market
necessity for incremental interstate transportation infrastructure.

competitive supply dynamics, and ensure the reliable delivery of natural gas to utilities, power

1.5.1     General Pipeline Construction Procedures

Construction of the proposed TL-669 pipeline will follow industry-standard practices and
procedures. In a typical scenario, construction involves a series of discrete activities conducted
in a linear sequence. These include survey and staking; clearing and grading; trenching; pipe
stringing, bending, and welding; lowering-in and backfilling; hydrostatic testing; final tie-in;
commissioning; and ROW cleanup and restoration. A description of each step in the process is
provided in the following sections.

Construction of the TL-668 pipeline will generally mimic the existing alignment of the LN-280
pipeline. The existing LN-280, and in some cases the LN-340 as well, will be removed first, and
then the new TL-668 pipeline will be installed in the same location as the removed pipeline,
commonly referred to as the “lift and lay” method. This process requires a specific construction
sequence to ensure that the removal and installation are completed in the safest, most practicable
manner, while minimizing disturbance and adhering to state and federal requirements. The “lift
and lay” method is further described below in Section 1.5.1.6.

1.5.1.1    Survey and Staking

Affected landowners will be notified before the preconstruction survey and staking are conducted.
After these notifications, the EGTS survey contractor will stake the pipeline centerlines and limits
of the construction ROW and ATWS areas. Wetland boundaries, E&S measures, and other
environmentally sensitive areas will also be marked at this time.

1.5.1.2    Clearing and Grading

Prior to beginning ground-disturbing activities, the EGTS construction contractors will coordinate
with the One-Call systems in PA to have existing underground utilities (e.g., cables, conduits, and
pipelines) identified and flagged. Once this process is complete, access to the ROW will be
constructed as needed, and the clearing crew will mobilize to the construction areas. Fences
along the ROW will be cut and braced, and temporary gates and fences will be installed to contain
livestock, if present and in accordance with landowner specifications. The clearing crew will then




                                                 -16-                               Project Stratum
                                                                                    November 2026
 clear the work area of vegetation and other obstacles, including trees, stumps, logs, brush, and
rocks.

EGTS will minimize tree removal to the extent practicable during pipeline construction, particularly
along TL-668 on State Forest lands. Cleared vegetation and stumps will either be burned, chipped
(except in wetlands), or hauled offsite to a commercial disposal facility. No chips, mulch, or
mechanically cut woody debris will be stockpiled in wetlands, and no upland woody debris will be
disposed of in wetlands. Marketable timber that is cleared will be managed in accordance with
the landowner agreements, with timber given back to the landowner or properly disposed (e.g.,
stacked along the edge of the LOD, chipped, or hauled to an approved disposal site). Non-
merchantable timber will not be disposed of by placing it off the ROW without landowner approval.
No woody debris disposal will be allowed in agricultural areas or wetlands.

Burning of non-merchantable wood will be allowed only where EGTS has acquired all applicable
permits and approvals (e.g., agency and landowner) and in accordance with state and local
regulations.

Following clearing, the construction ROW and ATWS will be graded where necessary to provide
a level work surface to allow safe passage of construction equipment and emergency vehicles.
Graded topsoil will be segregated in accordance with the FERC Plan and Procedures, where
required. Typically, topsoil will be segregated from subsoil in non-saturated wetlands, cultivated
or rotated croplands, managed pastures, hayfields, residential areas, and in other areas
requested by the landowner or land managing agency unless EGTS is instructed by a landowner
or land managing agency not to do so.

The depth of topsoil removed will depend on soil conditions and landowner requests or land
managing agency requirements. In accordance with the FERC Plan and Procedures, and in areas
where topsoil segregation is required, EGTS will segregate at least 12 inches of topsoil in deep
soils (more than 12 inches of topsoil) and the entire topsoil layer, A-horizon, in shallow soils (less
than 12 inches of topsoil).

If the ground is relatively flat and does not require topsoil segregation or grading, the existing
vegetative mat will be peeled and removed similar to topsoil and stockpiled along the ROW for
use in restoration. In areas disturbed by grading, and as required by the FERC Plan and
Procedures, temporary E&S measures will be installed along the ROW in conjunction with earth
disturbance to minimize erosion. The E&S measures will be inspected and maintained throughout
the construction and restoration phases of the Project, as appropriate, and as required by the
FERC Plan and Procedures.

1.5.1.3   Trenching

Pipe trench will be excavated by rotary trenching machines, track-mounted excavators, or other
similar equipment. Trench spoil will be deposited adjacent to the trench within the construction
ROW. The trench for the pipeline will be excavated to a depth that provides sufficient cover over
the pipeline after backfilling. The bottom width of the trench will be sufficient to accommodate the
diameter of the pipeline, safe access to construction personnel, and sufficient pad material around
it. The top width will vary to allow the sides of the trench to be adapted to local soil conditions at
the time of construction. Trench dewatering may be necessary to remove excess water from
excavations or ponded areas during periods of excessive precipitation or due to high water tables.
Dewatering activities will be performed in accordance with FERC Plan and Procedures and



                                                  -17-                                Project Stratum
                                                                                      November 2026
 applicable permits. Under no circumstances shall heavily silt-laden waters be directly discharged
into wetlands or waterbodies.

In areas where upland topsoil segregation is required, subsoil from trench excavations will be
placed adjacent to topsoil in a separate pile to allow for proper restoration of the soil during
backfilling and restoration. Gaps will be left between the topsoil and subsoil piles to prevent
stormwater runoff from backing up or flooding. Mixing of topsoil and subsoil piles will be prevented
by separating them physically or with a mulch or silt fence barrier, where necessary, to
accommodate reduced workspace.

When rock or rocky formations are encountered, hydraulic hammers, tractor-mounted mechanical
rippers or rock trenchers will be used for breaking up the rock prior to excavation. No blasting is
anticipated as part of the proposed Project.

1.5.1.4   Pipe Stringing, Bending, and Welding

Individual joints of pipe (typically procured in nominal 40-foot lengths) will be trucked to the
construction ROW and strung along the trench line, except at tie-ins near road crossings and
pipeline crossings. Individual sections of pipe will be bent, where necessary, to allow for a uniform
fit with the contours at the bottom of the trench and horizontal points of inflection. Typically, a
track-mounted, hydraulic pipe-bending machine will tailor the shape of the pipe to conform to the
contours of the trench. After the pipe sections are bent, they will be welded together into long
sections and placed on temporary supports along the trench. Factory-made elbows will be used
for changes in direction that exceed deflection specifications for the pipe, and as determined for
constructability.

Welding is a crucial phase of pipeline construction because the integrity of the pipeline depends
on this process. Welding will be conducted in compliance with approved welding procedures and
specifications. Completed welds will be visually and non-destructively inspected. Welds that do
not meet established specifications will be repaired or removed. Following welding and after
inspection, pipe weld joints will be coated with an epoxy coating in accordance with required
procedures and specifications. The coating will be inspected for defects, and repaired, if
necessary, prior to lowering the pipe into the trench.

1.5.1.5   Lowering-in and Backfilling

Prior to lowering-in, the trench will be inspected to confirm it is free of rocks and other debris that
could damage the pipe or its protective coating. Dewatering may be necessary to inspect the
bottom of the trench in areas where water has accumulated. If dewatering is required, it will be
conducted in accordance with the FERC Plan and Procedures and applicable permits in a manner
that will not cause erosion or result in silt-laden water flowing into a wetland or waterbody.

The pipe will be lifted from the temporary supports and lowered into the trench using side-boom
tractors or equivalent equipment. As necessary, trench breakers will be installed in the trench
around the pipe in steeply sloped areas to prevent movement of subsurface water along the
pipeline.

After lowering-in, the pipe will be padded and the trench will be backfilled with previously
excavated materials using bladed equipment or excavators, or mechanical padding equipment
and shaker buckets. If rock is present, shaker buckets or mechanical padding equipment will be


                                                   -18-                                Project Stratum
                                                                                       November 2026
 used to filter the rock from the backfill and rock shield may be installed on the pipe to prevent
damage. The rock may be pulverized and used as backfill, or other suitable fill will be installed
around the pipe. Excavated rock will then be used to backfill the trench to the top of the existing
bedrock profile in the trench. Excavated material not required for backfill will be removed and
disposed of at approved upland disposal sites or in accordance with landowner agreements.

If soils containing hazardous materials are encountered during excavation, EGTS will implement
the procedures required by local, state, and federal regulations.

1.5.1.6    Lift and Lay Method

After the construction ROW for the TL-668 pipeline has been grubbed, graded, and prepped, the
existing LN-280 pipeline will be excavated and removed, followed by temporary stabilization of
the trench and exposed soils. This sequencing is dictated by the constrained construction ROW
and the need to maintain safe construction practices. Following removal of the existing pipeline
along the proposed replacement alignment, a second mobilization will commence to install the
new TL-668 pipeline within the same general trench. Minor deviations from the existing pipeline
alignment may be necessary to accommodate current construction and safety practices and the
size and configuration of the new TL-668 pipeline. The construction ROW will be permanently
stabilized as installation progresses.

At waterbody and saturated or complex wetland crossings, removal and replacement of the
existing pipeline and permanent stabilization will be performed in a continuous sequence, to the
extent practicable, to minimize the duration of resource disturbance and the length of time the
trench remains open. Consistent with the FERC Procedures, the replacement section of TL-668
will be engineered, bent, welded, and coated outside the wetland or waterbody crossing area to
the extent practicable. Once the replacement pipe is prepared for installation, the existing pipeline
will be removed, the trench will be excavated, and the new pipeline will be lowered into the trench
and tied into the adjacent pipeline segments. The trench will then be backfilled and the crossing
restored in accordance with applicable permit conditions and the FERC Plan and Procedures.
This sequence will minimize the duration of open trenching within wetlands and waterbodies while
allowing the existing pipeline to remain in service until replacement activities are initiated.

During restoration, trench breakers and slope breakers will be installed where required or
approved by the applicable regulating agencies.

1.5.1.7   Hydrostatic Testing

After backfilling and all other construction activities for the TL-669 and TL-668 pipelines are
complete, the pipelines will be hydrostatically tested in sections to verify that the system is free
from leaks and will provide the required margin of safety at operating pressures. Individual
sections of the pipelines to be tested will be determined by water availability and terrain conditions.
Water for hydrostatic testing will be obtained from municipal sources in accordance with PA
regulations and required permits. As practicable, water will be transferred from one test section
to another to reduce the amount of water that is required for testing. Hydrostatic test water
disposal will be in accordance with federal, state, and local regulations after completion of the
test.

During hydrostatic testing, internal pressures and durations will be in accordance with 49 CFR 192
and applicable permit conditions. If leaks are found during testing, the leaks will be repaired and

 the section of pipe retested until the required specifications are met. Additional information on
hydrostatic testing is provided in Resource Report 2.

1.5.1.8    Final Tie-in and Commissioning

After hydrostatic testing, the final tie-ins on the pipelines will be completed and commissioning
will commence. Commissioning involves activities to verify that equipment is properly installed
and working, controls and communications systems are functional, and the pipeline or facility is
ready for service. The pipeline will be cleaned, dried, and inspected using in-line inspection tools
(pigs) to detect anomalies in the pipe that may have been introduced during construction, and
prepared for service by purging the line of air and loading the line with natural gas.

1.5.1.9    Clean Up and Restoration

Final cleanup will begin after backfilling and as soon as weather and site conditions permit. Final
cleanup (including final grading and installation of permanent E&S measures) will be completed
within timeframes as required by permits, in accordance with landowner requests, as required by
the FERC Plan and Procedures, or as approved by the appropriate agencies. Construction debris
will be collected and taken to an approved disposal facility. Preconstruction contours will be
restored as closely as practicable. Segregated upland topsoil will be spread over the surface of
the ROW, and permanent E&S measures will be installed.

Revegetation measures for all Project facilities will be implemented in accordance with the FERC
Plan and Procedures and the Post-Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM)/Site
Restoration Plans that will be prepared for the Project facilities and approved by PADEP, or in
accordance with applicable landowner agreements. Disturbed, non-cultivated work areas will be
stabilized and reseeded as soon as possible after final grading, weather and soil conditions
permitting, subject to the recommended seeding dates for the seed mixes used to revegetate
different areas along the pipelines. Reseeding will stabilize the soil, improve the appearance of
the area disturbed by construction, and in some cases, restore native flora.

Post-construction markers showing the location of the pipeline will be installed intermittently along
the pipeline ROWs according to EGTS specifications, state/federal regulations, and landowner
agreements. The markers will convey emergency information in accordance with applicable
government regulations, including USDOT safety requirements.

methods are provided in Appendix 1-E.

1.5.2.1    Wetland and Waterbody Crossings

The proposed TL-669 and TL-668 pipelines were routed and workspace planned to avoid or
minimize impacts to wetland and waterbody areas located in the vicinity of the proposed pipeline

FERC; and additional requirements identified in federal and/or state waterbody crossing permits,

and measures to prevent dewatering of the wetland resulting from trenching activities. These
measures will limit the duration that wetland soils are exposed. Appropriate BMPs will be
implemented to protect the wetlands during and between construction activities and during
restoration. Backfilling and stabilization of the wetlands will commence immediately after
installation of the new pipeline.

1.5.2.2   Road Crossings

The proposed Project will not cross highways or railroads. Construction across paved roads will
be conducted in accordance with the FERC Plan and requirements identified in road crossing
permits or approvals. Most paved roads will be crossed either by conventional boring beneath the
roadbed or open-cut method. Boring activities will consist of excavating a pit on each side of the
roadway and horizontally drilling or pushing the pipeline through from one pit to the other without
disturbing the surface above the pipeline. Typically, there is little or no disruption to traffic at road
crossings during boring operations.

For local or township roads, unpaved roads, two-tracks, trails, and driveways, as well as roads in
areas with a high-water table, the open-cut crossing method will be used and the road will then
be restored to preconstruction conditions. This method could require temporary closure of the
road, two-track, or trail to traffic and establishment of detours. For roads, if no reasonable detour
is feasible, at least one lane of the road being crossed will be kept open to traffic, except during
brief periods when it is essential to close the road to install the pipeline in the trench. Most open-
cut road crossings will be completed and the road restored in a few days using the same type of
sub-bed and surface material as the original construction. EGTS will take measures such as
posting signs and implementing necessary traffic control measures at open-cut road crossings for
safety and to minimize traffic disruptions. Debris from road construction (e.g., remnants of
concrete) will be recycled or disposed of at an approved disposal facility.
